text:
Lina (AE): Heads-up-- FedHealth POC wants an accelerated sign. They need an orderform + DPA with export-control carveouts and a special SLA for on-prem deployment. procurement insists on PO then invoice. can we map signers?
Tom (Sales Ops): Got it. Do we have the final order form? I only see OF_v5 (prepay) and OF_v6 (net30). Which one is the customer expecting?
Lina (AE): They confirmed net30 in the procurement questionnaire but finance is pushing for prepay for on-prem deployments. negotiation point.
Priya (Legal): @Lina can you confirm whether FedHealth requires FedRAMP-like attestation or just an export-control clause? that determines whether we need additional audit language in the DPA.
Lina (AE): their security contact wrote: "no FedRAMP cert required for POC, but data cannot leave the physical host and export-control clause mandatory. KMS/HSM preferred."
Diego (Solutions): On-prem POC + HSM = possible, but latency SLA will be tighter. If we promise 99.9% for private infra we need a Dedicated commit and runbook + in-region engineers. That affects pricing.
Tom (Sales Ops): Who signs? Typical flow we use: procurement stamps PO, then exec sign for MSAs with custom indemnities. Customer asked for procurement-first; they want to attach PO number to DocuSign.
Priya (Legal): I reviewed OF_v6 (net30). Redlines needed: add export-control paragraph, limit indemnity for subprocessor breaches, and add KMS scoping. Also need clause: customer may require onsite audit with 48h notice (we should limit to remote review only). I'll propose remote-only with 7-day notice.
Lina (AE): Procurement contact: procurement@fedhealth.gov and signer is "Jane D (Procurement)". Exec sig requested by CISO but they said it could be stamping if legal accepts DPA appendix.
Tom (Sales Ops): I'll prepare DocuSign envelope: tag procurement as signer 1 (stamp), exec as signer 2 (optional). Which orderform version to attach?
Priya (Legal): Attach OF_v6 but add a countersign checkbox: "Exec signature required if customer requests changes to indemnity or export-control". That allows stamp-only flow for standard DPA.
Diego (Solutions): Note: if they insist HSM, on-prem kit lead time ~10 days. We should flag go-live schedule in the order form.
BillingBot (bot): Draft invoice created: https://billing.redwood.internal/drafts/FED-PO-2026-11 (internal)
Tom (Sales Ops): Sending envelope now. PO field prefilled with PO: FED-PO-2026-11. routing: procurement -> legal acknowledgement -> exec(optional).
Priya (Legal): Uploaded DPA redline with export-control paragraph and remote-audit language: https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/attachment/99999/FedHealth_DPA_redline.docx. Summary: export-control carveout, KMS scope, audit remote-only, indemnity cap tied to fees.
Lina (AE): @Priya can we accept indemnity cap = contract value? customer asked for higher. procurement will only stamp if cap <= PO amount.
Priya (Legal): For PO <= $200k we can accept cap = fees; above that need exec sign.
Tom (Sales Ops): Envelope status: sent to procurement. ETA 24h. I'll escalate to Jane if no response in 8h.
Diego (Solutions): Pricing note: Dedicated/on-prem surcharge + HSM provisioning = +40% for POC month. Need approval from pricing.
BillingBot (bot): Reminder queued: send final invoice when envelope complete.
Lina (AE): Thanks team. I'll follow up with FedHealth CISO for exec availability if procurement stamps. Keep me posted. :handshake:
Tom (Sales Ops): Noted. Ping me if procurement asks for a different PO format.
Priya (Legal): I'll stand by to approve final countersign or to route for exec signature if they escalate.
Lina (AE): Closing plan: procurement stamp should suffice per Priya for PO <= $200k. pushing for net30. will update thread after stamp.
